analysis.title: Prime Services Weekly Report, November 13, 2026 (Friday 11/6 – Thursday 11/12)
key_insights: GS Equity Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate rose +1.16% for 11/6-11/12 vs MSCI World TR +2.34%, driven by beta of +1.45%, partly offset by alpha of -0.29% on long side losses.
GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate rose +1.42% over the same week, driven by alpha of +1.56% on short side gains, partly offset by beta of -0.15%.

Overall book gross leverage fell 2.1 pts to 312.1% (74th percentile 1-year) and net leverage fell 0.4 pts to 71.4% (3rd percentile 1-year). Overall L/S ratio rose 0.1% to 1.593 (4th percentile 1-year).

Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 2.6 pts to 208.4% (34th percentile 1-year) and net leverage rose 0.1 pts to 45.4%, a 1-year low. Beta-adjusted fundamental gross rose 6.0 pts to 222.6% (11th percentile) and beta-adjusted net fell 0.2 pts to 57.0%, a 1-year low.
Global equities were net sold (-0.7 SDs 1-year) as de-grossing continued to increase, with long sales outpacing short covers 2.8 to 1.
All regions except Europe were net sold, led by EM Asia and North America.

Single stocks were net sold for a 9th straight week, driven by long sales and to a lesser extent short sales. Macro products were net bought for a 4th straight week, driven by short covers and to a lesser extent long buys.
9 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Health Care and Financials. Energy and Real Estate were the only net bought sectors.

Health Care was among the most $ net sold and the most risk-off global sector, net sold for a 4th straight week at the fastest pace in over 7 months, driven entirely by long sales. Biotech, Pharmaceuticals and HC Providers & Services led subsector selling.

The Prime book is overweight Health Care vs MSCI World by +6.0% (67th percentile 1-year, 93rd percentile 5-year). Gross/net allocation is 11.9%/15.5% (82nd/97th percentile 1-year, 50th/84th percentile 5-year).

Energy was the most $ net bought and most risk-on global sector, net bought for the first time in 5 weeks and at the fastest pace in 3 months, with long buys outpacing short sales 7 to 1. Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels drove the buying, led by North America long buys.

The Prime book is overweight Energy vs MSCI World by +0.5% (90th percentile 1-year, 74th percentile 5-year). Gross/net allocation is 4.8%/4.6% (79th/85th percentile 1-year, 34th/49th percentile 5-year).

The largest regional flow changes were AEJ long sales of -2.74 SDs and Europe short covers of +1.57 SDs. The largest sector flow changes were Health Care long sales of -2.16 SDs and Staples short sales of -1.53 SDs.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds net sold the sector for a 4th straight week at the fastest pace in over 7 months, entirely long sales. This is positioning flow, not a formal rating.
Net bought at the fastest pace in 3 months, driven by long buys outpacing short sales 7 to 1. This is positioning flow, not a formal rating.
Led global sector net selling in dollar terms. This is positioning flow, not a formal rating.

risk_factors: Continued de-grossing with long sales outpacing short covers at 2.8 to 1.
Prime book overweight Health Care by +6.0% vs MSCI World (93rd percentile 5-year) while funds sell the sector at the fastest pace in over 7 months.
Fundamental net leverage at 1-year lows leaves less exposure to a rally.
vol_and_positioning: Overall book net leverage of 71.4% is in the 3rd percentile over 1 year, and the overall L/S ratio of 1.593 is in the 4th percentile.
Fundamental L/S net leverage of 45.4% and beta-adjusted net leverage of 57.0% are both 1-year lows.
Global equity flows were -0.7 SDs (1-year), with long sales outpacing short covers 2.8 to 1.
Single stocks were net sold for a 9th straight week while macro products were net bought for a 4th straight week.
Weekly market table: VIX level 22.8 (WoW +1.6 pp), NYSE volume 28.18 (WoW +63.8%), SPX realized correlation 22.8% (listed column order is ambiguous), 10Y UST 5.1% (WoW +0.27 pp).
